label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, money-unit, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, offered one write action (rollback_deploy), which runs only if a person approves it at the gate, and stopped on diagnosed after 6 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Klaxon asked at the approval gate to act on its diagnosis; the request was approved with make approve (the request's id typed at a terminal), and the action ran: redeploy payments-api: PROVIDER_BREAKER on (unchanged), CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT dollars -> cents, REFUND_CONNECTION returned (unchanged). Code, not the model, then verified it (klaxon.agent.verify): passed; the cause is removed, and the money is not right. The fault's cause was removed by Klaxon: its rollback (Klaxon, approved request r-742c) removed the cause, and the harness's clearing then found the good settings running, and changed nothing.

fault.name: money-unit
fault.title: Customers charged 100 times the amount: a money-unit bug
fault.cause: a deploy of the payments API with a money-unit bug (CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars): it reads each payment's amount, already in cents, as dollars and converts it to cents again, so the provider charges every customer 100 times the amount, while our own records keep the right one
expected_symptoms: the money check fails on payments_match_provider, at the first evaluation after the deploy: for each payment since, the provider charged 100 times our amount ('amount differs')
the ledger books what the provider charged, so it agrees with the provider, and the other invariants pass
the payment confirmer logs a conflict for each such payment: the provider charged a different amount than our payment's

a payment whose answer was lost during the fault stays pending for good ('pending but charged, amount differs'): the confirmer refuses the provider's 100 times amount; its client's retries raise the p95 of POST /payments to about 0.6 s, under its threshold
the API stays healthy, and its answers show the right amount
refunds send the right amount: a full refund gives back 1% of what was charged
fault.remedy: roll the payments API back to CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents, then refund each customer charged since the deploy what was charged above the amount, at the provider: our API refunds no more than our recorded amount (a write, so it needs approval)

diagnosis.hypothesis: payments-api was redeployed at 08:27:01Z with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. Since then it sends our amount in cents to fake-provider as if it were dollars, so the provider charges 100x what we recorded. The first affected payment is pmt_000230: we recorded 1291 cents and the provider charged 129100. Every payment after the deploy is overcharged this way, which produces the payments_match_provider findings. The ledger books what the provider reports, so the ledger still matches the provider and stays balanced, but customers are overcharged against our records.

evidence.shows: payments_match_provider failed with 63 findings, all starting at pmt_000230. The provider's amount is exactly 100x ours (for example 1291 against 129100 cents). The other four invariants pass. pmt_000233 is still pending on our side but charged at 100x.
payments-api is the newest deploy, at 08:27:01Z, with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. Every other service was created at 08:25:26Z.
pmt_000230, the first flagged payment, succeeded at 08:27:02.413Z, just after the deploy. We logged amount_cents=1291.

pmt_000230's trace shows payments-api inserting the payment and then POSTing to fake-provider /v1/payments with a 200 reply. The request body is not shown, so the amount actually sent is inferred from the provider's record.
pmt_000229, the last payment the check did not flag, succeeded at 08:27:00.655Z, just before the deploy. This ties the start of the overcharges to the deploy.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll payments-api back to the settings it ran before the 08:27:01Z deploy, presumably CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents. That stops new 100x charges. Afterwards, refund the overcharged difference for pmt_000230 onward, or the full charge if refunding and re-charging is simpler, and correct the ledger. Check pmt_000233, which is pending on our side but charged at the provider, and settle its status.

diagnosis.blast_radius: Recreating payments-api pauses payment and refund intake for a few seconds. Requests in flight during the restart may fail and be retried under their idempotency keys. The rollback repairs nothing: the roughly 63 overcharged payments stay wrong until a separate repair. The previous settings are not shown in c2, so the rollback assumes the earlier value was cents.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rollback makes things worse, redeploy payments-api with the settings from the 08:27:01Z deploy (PROVIDER_BREAKER=on, CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars, REFUND_CONNECTION=returned). Then run money_check again to confirm that new payments match the provider.
